# Medical
Medical is responsible for the health, wellbeing, and mental welfare of station personnel.
## Medical Roles
[bold][color=#ffffff]Position[/color][/bold]
[bold][color=#ffffff]Purpose[/color][/bold]
[textlink="Chief Medical Officer" link="SOPCMO"]
Oversees the Medical Department, coordinates patient care, manages medical personnel, and ensures proper medical procedures are followed.
Paramedic
Responds to medical emergencies, retrieves injured personnel, provides emergency treatment, and transports patients to Medical.
Geneticist
Studies genetics, performs genetic modifications and treatments, and assists in the diagnosis and correction of genetic abnormalities.
Chemist
Manufactures medicines, medical compounds, and other approved chemicals required for patient care and station operations.
Medical Doctor
Diagnoses illnesses and injuries, treats patients, performs routine medical care, and helps maintain the overall health of the crew.
Medical Intern
Assists Medical personnel with patient care and departmental duties while learning the responsibilities of the Medical Department.
Psychologist
Provides mental health support, counseling, and emotional care to crew members experiencing stress, trauma, or other psychological concerns.
## Department Expectations
- Medical personnel are expected to provide care to those who need it regardless of personal feelings, departmental affiliation, or social status.
- Patients should be treated with professionalism, respect, and dignity whenever possible.
- Medical staff should make reasonable efforts to preserve life and minimize unnecessary harm.
- Confidential medical information should remain confidential unless disclosure is required for safety, legal, or operational reasons.
- Chemists, Doctors, Psychologists, and Paramedics should cooperate to provide effective care rather than operating as entirely separate groups.
- Medical is encouraged to roleplay injuries, treatment, recovery, mental health, and long-term care rather than reducing every patient interaction to mechanical treatment.
## Final Note
Medical exists to preserve life and care for the crew. Professionalism, compassion, and cooperation are just as important as medical knowledge.
